data.name: Gwenore
data.long_meaning: Gwenore is a name of Celtic origin, derived from the Welsh words 'gwen' (fair, white, beautiful) and 'ore' (maiden, virgin). In Welsh mythology, Gwenore was the name of a sea goddess, representing the maiden form of the sea god, Gorre. In Christian tradition, it is a name associated with purity, innocence, and devotion to the Virgin Mary.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes purity, innocence, and devotion to the divine feminine.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gwenore holds significant cultural importance in Wales, particularly in the realm of Celtic mythology. It is a name deeply rooted in Welsh history and folklore, representing the connection between the sea and spirituality. This name may evoke images of the undulating shores of Wales' coastline, and the ancient stories of the sea deities who are said to inhabit the waters.

It symbolizes the inherent beauty and purity within each individual, as well as the deep connection to the divine feminine. As a name associated with the Virgin Mary, it can serve as a constant reminder of the power of devotion, faith, and innocence.
